items.title: Term neonate, awake (activite moyenne)
items.caption: Term neonate (40 weeks) awake: continuous low-to-medium voltage mixed delta and theta in all regions (activite moyenne), with no posterior dominant rhythm and no interburst periods. Muscle over the right temporal chains and an eye movement at 2 s.

items.title: Infant (6 months), awake
items.caption: Six-month-old awake, eyes closed: a 5-6 Hz posterior rhythm, largest in T5-O1, P3-O1, T6-O2 and P4-O2, over mixed theta and delta.

items.title: Toddler (2 years), awake
items.caption: Two-year-old awake, eyes closed: a 6-7 Hz posterior rhythm in the occipital and parietal chains with intermixed theta; lower-voltage faster activity in the frontal derivations.

items.title: Child (8 years), eyes closed: posterior dominant rhythm
items.caption: Eight-year-old awake, eyes closed: symmetric 8–9 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, with lower-voltage frontal activity and a brief burst of temporal muscle artifact.

items.title: Adolescent, awake
items.caption: Adolescent awake, eyes closed: a 9.5–10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, waxing and waning in the posterior derivations, with a clear anterior-posterior gradient.

items.title: Adult, awake
items.caption: Adult awake, eyes closed: a low-voltage 10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm in the posterior derivations with little slow activity.

items.title: Posterior rhythm reactivity to eye opening
items.caption: Child awake: the 8.5 Hz posterior rhythm attenuates with the frontopolar eye-opening deflection near 8 s. Later blinks are visible; the background is reactive.

items.title: Hyperventilation build-up
items.caption: Child near the end of 3 minutes of hyperventilation: diffuse, irregular 1.5-3 Hz delta, largest frontally (Fp1-F3, Fp2-F4), mixed with the waking background. Symmetric; a normal build-up in a child.

items.title: Photic driving at 12 Hz
items.caption: Photic stimulation at 12 flashes per second (Photic channel, 3-13 s): a 12 Hz occipital response time-locked to the flashes, symmetric and maximal in P3-O1, P4-O2, T5-O1 and T6-O2, stopping with the train.

items.title: Drowsiness
items.caption: Child falling asleep: the posterior rhythm visible early in the page becomes less prominent around 9–10 s and gives way to lower-voltage mixed theta as drowsiness develops.

items.title: N1: vertex waves
items.caption: Adolescent in N1: sharply contoured vertex waves, maximal at Cz, with phase reversals in Fz-Cz/Cz-Pz and the central parasagittal chains, over low-voltage theta.

items.title: N2: sleep spindles
items.caption: Child in N2: bilateral waxing and waning sleep spindles at 12–14 Hz, lasting about 1–2 s, with centroparietal prominence and lower-voltage spread to the temporal chains.

items.title: N2: K-complexes
items.caption: Adolescent in N2: frontocentral K-complexes with an initial sharp negative wave followed by a slower positive wave. A central sleep spindle follows the first completed complex.

items.title: Infant N2: long asynchronous spindles
items.caption: Six-month-old in N2: long spindle trains lasting several seconds, independently prominent over each hemisphere. Asynchronous and overlapping spindles are normal at this age.

items.title: N3: slow-wave sleep
items.caption: Child in N3: diffuse high-voltage 0.5–2 Hz slow waves, prominent in the frontocentral chains and smaller posteriorly, on a mixed sleep background.

items.title: REM sleep
items.caption: Adolescent in an authored REM interval: low-voltage mixed-frequency cerebral activity without spindles or K-complexes, with bursts of opposing frontotemporal rapid eye movement deflections.

items.title: REM: sawtooth waves
items.caption: Adult in an authored REM interval (5 uV/mm): a brief 2–4 Hz sawtooth train, maximal centrally and at the vertex, precedes a burst of opposing frontotemporal eye movements.

items.title: Arousal from N2
items.caption: Child arousal from an authored N2 interval: a slower mixed sleep background and a frontocentral K-complex just before 6 s precede the shift to faster activity, frontotemporal muscle and movement.

items.title: Mu rhythm
items.caption: Right-predominant mu rhythm: sustained, waxing and waning 10 Hz arciform activity over the right sensorimotor region, mixed with the awake background; much smaller on the left. No ictal evolution or after-going slow wave.

items.title: Lambda waves
items.caption: Lambda waves during visual scanning: repeated surface-positive, sail-like occipital transients in P3-O1, P4-O2, T5-O1 and T6-O2, with blinks and other evidence of wakefulness; no posterior dominant rhythm.

items.title: Posterior slow waves of youth
items.caption: Posterior slow waves of youth, eyes closed: isolated 2.5–4 Hz waves fused with the 9 Hz posterior rhythm in the occipital derivations. A normal finding in children and adolescents.

items.title: Hypnagogic hypersynchrony
items.caption: Hypnagogic hypersynchrony on a slower, higher-voltage drowsy background. The wider window shows the lead-in before the high-voltage frontocentral delta-theta burst, followed by return to the drowsy background.

items.title: Positive occipital sharp transients of sleep (POSTS)
items.caption: Occasional surface-positive occipital sharp transients in N2, separated by irregular intervals rather than a nearly continuous train; a normal sleep finding.

items.title: Wicket waves
items.caption: Low-amplitude 7-9 Hz arciform temporal runs and single wicket waves in drowsiness, with no after-going slow wave or ictal evolution.

items.title: Rhythmic mid-temporal theta of drowsiness (RMTD)
items.caption: RMTD in drowsiness: independent runs of rhythmic, notched 5–6 Hz theta over the left and right mid-temporal chains, without evolution in frequency or field.

items.title: 14 and 6 Hz positive bursts
items.caption: 14 and 6 Hz positive bursts in light sleep (ear reference): brief positive comb-like bursts, at 6–7 Hz on the left and 14 Hz on the right, with a posterior temporal/occipital maximum.

items.title: Frontal arousal rhythm
items.caption: Child arousing from N2: a quieter mixed-frequency sleep background precedes arousal with frontotemporal muscle at 5 s. Independently waxing rhythmic 8 Hz trains follow in the frontal and frontocentral chains, with smaller posterior spread.

items.title: SREDA
items.caption: SREDA onset in an authored awake adult interval: sharply contoured slowing builds into sustained 5–6 Hz activity with a posterior maximum and left predominance. This page shows the onset of a simulated 60-s run.

items.title: Eye blinks
items.caption: Symmetric bifrontal deflections maximal in Fp1-F3/Fp2-F4 and Fp1-F7/Fp2-F8, each with a fast rise and a slightly slower return, fading by F3-C3. Posterior chains are unaffected.

items.title: Lateral eye movements
items.caption: Box-shaped deflections of opposite polarity at F7 and F8: Fp1-F7 and F7-T3 deflect in opposite directions (phase reversal at F7), mirrored on the right, so the two sides are always opposed. Each saccade rises in tens of milliseconds and returns through the low-frequency filter.

items.title: Slow roving eye movements of drowsiness
items.caption: Irregular slow lateral eye movements (half-waves of about 1-2 s) in Fp1-F7 and Fp2-F8, opposite in F7-T3/F8-T4 and opposed between the two sides, in drowsiness as the posterior rhythm drops out; vertex waves appear in the parasagittal chains.

items.title: REM eye movements
items.caption: Clusters of rapid conjugate eye movements in REM sleep: steep opposite-polarity deflections at F7 and F8 in groups of 2-4 over 1-2 s, on a low-voltage mixed-frequency background without posterior alpha.

items.title: Chewing (EMG) artifact
items.caption: Rhythmic bursts of high-frequency muscle potentials at about 1-2 Hz, maximal in the temporal chains (Fp1-F7 to T5-O1 and Fp2-F8 to T6-O2), obscuring the background during each jaw closure.

items.title: Glossokinetic artifact
items.caption: Irregular 1-3 Hz slow potentials from tongue movement, in phase over both hemispheres and broad, from the frontotemporal to the posterior chains, unlike the opposed field of lateral eye movements. It can mimic diffuse delta; its irregularity and lack of evolution help.

items.title: Electrode pop
items.caption: Abrupt vertical deflections with exponential decay confined to the two derivations that share T5 (T3-T5 and T5-O1, mirror images), with no field in neighbouring chains.

items.title: 60 Hz interference
items.caption: With the notch filter off, a dense uniform 60 Hz band thickens the traces of the derivations that contain the high-impedance electrodes (here Fp2, F3 and C4); derivations without them are clean.

items.title: ECG artifact
items.caption: A small sharp transient on every beat, time-locked to the QRS in the ECG channel, clearest in the posterior and midline chains (T5-O1, P3-O1, Cz-Pz, C4-P4). Its regularity and fixed relation to the QRS mark it as artifact.

items.title: Pulse artifact
items.caption: A smooth slow wave filling each R-R interval at one electrode (Cz): Fz-Cz and Cz-Pz are mirror images, every other chain is clean, and each wave follows the QRS in the ECG channel by a fixed delay.

items.title: Sweat artifact
items.caption: Very slow (2-4 s) baseline sway in the right frontopolar chains (Fp2-F8, Fp2-F4, F4-C4), with the posterior chains unaffected; it remains visible with the 1 Hz low-frequency filter.

items.title: Movement artifact
items.caption: Abrupt, irregular high-amplitude transients over one region at a time, with electrode-to-electrode differences and co-timed muscle; posterior chains stay quiet. The lack of a consistent field or evolution separates it from cerebral activity.

items.title: Patting artifact
items.caption: Rhythmic 1-4 Hz slow transients from patting, in bouts, maximal posterior-temporal and parasagittal with a phase reversal at T5/T6; the background between bouts is unchanged.

items.title: Chest physiotherapy artifact
items.caption: Rhythmic 3 Hz waves from chest percussion, most prominent in Fp2-F8 and throughout the page, perfectly regular and without evolution, in an ICU infant.

items.title: Ventilator artifact
items.caption: A brief burst of 5-12 Hz oscillation with every breath at a fixed rate (0.4 Hz, 24/min), focal in Fp1-F7 with a smaller homologous copy, parasagittal chains clean.

items.title: ECMO pump artifact
items.caption: Continuous monotonous rhythmic activity at the pump rate (about 1.5 Hz) in the derivations containing C4 (F4-C4 and C4-P4, mirror images), with no evolution in frequency, amplitude or field, in a neonate on ECMO.

items.title: Propofol - frontal alpha
items.caption: Propofol: frontally predominant alpha with large frontal slow waves beneath it, the anesthetic pattern, on a slower background.

items.title: Benzodiazepine beta (midazolam)
items.caption: Diffuse waxing and waning 14-20 Hz beta dominates every chain after midazolam, exceeding alpha; the posterior rhythm and blinks are absent.

items.title: Dexmedetomidine spindles
items.caption: A sleep-like slow background with 11-15 Hz spindle-like bursts of 1-2 s, frontocentral, at irregular intervals, resembling N2 spindles; no posterior dominant rhythm.

items.title: Ketamine - theta and gamma
items.caption: Ketamine increases theta and adds low-voltage 25-32 Hz gamma that alternates with slow-delta epochs; alpha and the posterior rhythm are absent.

items.title: Remifentanil - awake features preserved
items.caption: With an opioid alone the patient remains awake: the posterior dominant rhythm and blinks persist, with only a modest shift toward slower frequencies.

items.title: Barbiturate fast activity
items.caption: Before any discontinuity, pentobarbital adds diffuse 13-16 Hz fast activity over slower background; occipital alpha and blinks are gone.

items.title: Burst suppression on pentobarbital
items.caption: Pentobarbital titrated to 60 % suppression: 1-2 s bursts of polyphasic sharp and slow waves separated by irregular suppressions below 10 uV that still carry low-voltage residual activity.

items.title: Burst suppression on propofol
items.caption: Deep propofol with a high suppression target: irregular 1-2 s bursts of sharp, alpha and slow activity separated by suppressions below 10 uV.

items.title: Seizure under neuromuscular blockade
items.caption: A left hemispheric seizure 30 s after onset in a paralysed child: rhythmic 4-6 Hz activity over the left temporal and parasagittal chains, building in amplitude, free of the muscle artifact a clinical seizure would carry. Blockade removes scalp EMG only; the cerebral discharge is unchanged.

items.title: Focal polymorphic delta, left temporal
items.caption: Irregular 1-3 Hz polymorphic delta confined to the left temporal chain (Fp1-F7, F7-T3, T3-T5) with the parasagittal chains and the right side preserved - a regional structural abnormality.

items.title: Generalized slowing
items.caption: Diffuse continuous 2-4 Hz delta-theta activity over both hemispheres with no posterior dominant rhythm, in a child with encephalopathy; the background remains reactive.

items.title: Hemispheric attenuation (asymmetry)
items.caption: Persistently lower voltage across every derivation of the right hemisphere (about half the left), without added slowing; the posterior rhythm is reduced on the same side.

items.title: Abrupt regional attenuation (ischemia)
items.caption: Ten seconds into the page the left hemisphere abruptly loses voltage and its faster frequencies (F7-T3, T3-T5, C3-P3 and Fp1-F7 thin out over about 6 s) while some delta is spared, as in acute ischemia; the right hemisphere is unchanged.

items.title: Breach effect
items.caption: Over a left central skull defect (C3 and neighbours) the background is about twice the voltage of the homologous right side, with accentuated sharply contoured beta; this should not be read as epileptiform.

items.title: Low-voltage background
items.caption: Continuous but mostly below 20 uV in every derivation, a featureless mixed slow background with no posterior dominant rhythm, unreactive.

items.title: Suppressed background
items.caption: All activity below 10 uV throughout the page, featureless and unreactive; shown at the higher sensitivity of 3 uV/mm, where only low-amplitude residual activity is seen.

items.title: Burst suppression (encephalopathy)
items.caption: Generalized bursts of mixed slow and sharp activity separated by suppressions below 10 uV occupying most of the page, in an unreactive child without sedation.

items.title: Discontinuous background (child)
items.caption: Periods of attenuation interrupt an otherwise slow background for a minority of the page (ACNS discontinuous: 10-49 % attenuation or suppression), in an encephalopathic child.

items.title: Cyclic alternating pattern of encephalopathy
items.caption: The background alternates between an attenuated phase and a higher-voltage slow phase every 20 s (40 s cycle); this 30-s page starts in the attenuated phase and the higher-voltage phase returns at about 13 s. The pattern repeats for more than six cycles (ACNS CAPE).

items.title: Spindle coma
items.caption: Frontocentral 12-14 Hz spindles, vertex waves and K-complexes near 13 s and 19 s in an unresponsive child. Unreactivity and absent sleep-wake cycling are clinical and longer-record context for this synthetic example.

items.title: Alpha coma
items.caption: Diffuse, frontally predominant, monotonous alpha-frequency activity with no posterior dominant rhythm, low variability and no reactivity, in a comatose adolescent.

items.title: Therapeutic hypothermia
items.caption: Cooling from 36.5 to 33 C between 10 and 30 minutes fades the alpha band and the alpha/delta ratio falls from about 1 to 0.45. The page, at target temperature, is lower in voltage and slower, with little posterior dominant rhythm.

lines: FFT power: dB, using this image’s range and palette.
Spectrogram vertical axes: frequency in Hz.
Alpha/delta ratio: unitless.
Raw EEG calibration bar: 50 µV vertical · 1 second horizontal.
Trend time follows the labeled horizontal axis; raw EEG excerpts use seconds.

items.title: Left temporal spike with after-going slow wave
items.caption: Abundant (about one per 5 s) spikes at T3, each followed by a slow wave, phase-reversing at T3 between F7-T3 and T3-T5, on an awake child background with temporal muscle artifact.

items.title: Right temporal spike without after-going slow wave
items.caption: Brief spikes (<70 ms) at T4 with no after-going slow wave, phase-reversing at T4 between F8-T4 and T4-T6, in N2 sleep (vertex wave at 6.6 s, spindle at 9 s).

items.title: Right anterior temporal sharp waves (F8)
items.caption: Sharp waves (70-200 ms) with an after-going slow wave, maximal at F8, phase-reversing between Fp2-F8 and F8-T4 in the right temporal chain (3, 5.3, 7 and 10 s), in N2 sleep; the diffuse transient at 8.8 s is a vertex wave.

items.title: Right mesial temporal spike on T1/T2 montage
items.caption: Right mesial (subtemporal) temporal spikes on the longitudinal montage with T1/T2: the phase reversal is at T2 (F8-T2 against T2-T4), with smaller deflections in Fp2-F8 and T4-T6; the standard temporal chain alone would under-show them.

items.title: Left frontal spike
items.caption: Spikes with an after-going slow wave maximal at F3, phase-reversing at F3 between Fp1-F3 and F3-C3 in the left parasagittal chain, with a smaller field at F7 and Fz, in N2 sleep.

items.title: Left central spike
items.caption: Spikes maximal at C3, phase-reversing at C3 between F3-C3 and C3-P3 (several independent discharges across the page), with little involvement of the temporal chain, in N2 sleep.

items.title: Centrotemporal spikes activated in sleep (SeLECTS)
items.caption: Abundant right centrotemporal spikes in N2 sleep, phase-reversing at C4 (F4-C4 / C4-P4) and at T4 (F8-T4 / T4-T6), with a horizontal dipole (frontal positivity). Sleep spindles and vertex waves are present.

items.title: Left occipital spike
items.caption: Spikes maximal at O1, seen at the ends of the left temporal (T5-O1) and parasagittal (P3-O1) chains: with no electrode beyond O1 there is no phase reversal, and the focus is read from the end-of-chain maximum.

items.title: Right central polyspikes
items.caption: Polyspikes (brief trains of several spikes) with an after-going slow wave, maximal at C4 and seen across the right parasagittal chain (Fp2-F4 to P4-O2) in N2 sleep; a sleep spindle runs at 8-10 s.

items.title: Multifocal independent spikes
items.caption: Independent spikes from four foci (T3, F4, O2, C3), each with its own field and firing at different times, in N2 sleep: multifocal independent sporadic discharges.

items.title: Right temporal spike, referential montage
items.caption: The same kind of T4 spike on a referential (ear) montage: the discharge is largest at T4 and falls off at F8 and T6, with no phase reversal; amplitude, not reversal, localizes it here. The large diffuse wave at 2.4 s is a vertex wave of N2 sleep.

items.title: BIRDs, right temporal
items.caption: A 4-5 Hz rhythmic run lasting about 7 s over the right temporal chain (F8-T4 / T4-T6), shorter than 10 s and without evolution: BIRDs (possible), on a slow ICU background.

items.title: Definite BIRDs with evolution
items.caption: A brief (<10 s) left temporal run that changes in frequency and voltage during the run: BIRDs with evolution (definite BIRDs).

items.title: Left mesial temporal seizure onset
items.caption: Onset of a left mesial temporal seizure at 3 s: rhythmic 7 Hz theta that is present from the first ictal second, maximal in Fp1-F7 and F7-T3 (anterior temporal), without a low-voltage fast onset, slowing slightly over the page.

items.title: Right neocortical temporal seizure onset
items.caption: Right neocortical temporal onset: low-voltage fast activity appears over T4 (F8-T4, T4-T6) at about 3 s, then slows and builds into a 5-6 Hz rhythmic run in the right temporal chain by 10-20 s.

items.title: Temporal seizure evolution (30 s)
items.caption: The first 28 s of a left temporal seizure on one 30-s page: low-voltage fast activity in the left temporal chain becomes rhythmic 6-7 Hz activity, then slows toward 3 Hz while its voltage roughly triples: evolution in frequency and amplitude, the feature that separates a seizure from a rhythmic pattern.

items.title: Left frontal seizure onset
items.caption: Left frontal onset: at 5 s the left frontal region attenuates (electrodecrement) and carries low-voltage fast activity in Fp1-F7, F7-T3 and F3-C3; at 9-10 s high-voltage rhythmic activity builds over the left frontal and temporal chains.

items.title: Left central seizure (rhythmic spikes)
items.caption: Abrupt onset at 5 s of rhythmic 5-6 Hz sharply contoured activity at C3, phase-reversing between F3-C3 and C3-P3 and building in voltage over the next seconds, with little spread to the temporal chain; the seizure has a focal clonic correlate.

items.title: Right occipital seizure onset
items.caption: Right occipital onset at 5.5 s: fast rhythmic spiky activity at O2 at the ends of the right temporal and parasagittal chains (T6-O2, P4-O2), slowing to theta and building over the following seconds.

items.title: Right parietal seizure onset
items.caption: Right parietal onset at 5.5 s: low-voltage fast activity at P4 (C4-P4, P4-O2, T4-T6) that slows into rhythmic theta and builds in voltage over the right parasagittal chain.

items.title: Focal to bilateral spread
items.caption: A right temporal seizure already in progress recruits the right hemisphere and then the left, with increasing voltage and muscle artifact. This 30-second page spans the transition toward bilateral activity.

items.title: Postictal regional attenuation
items.caption: The end of a left temporal seizure: the rhythmic 2 Hz run in the left temporal chain stops at about 7 s and is followed by lower-voltage, slower activity over the left temporal region (T3-T5, T5-O1) compared with the right.

items.title: Electrographic focal status epilepticus
items.caption: Continuous left temporal rhythmic 2-4 Hz ictal activity in a comatose patient with no clinical correlate, ten minutes into a 20-minute run: electrographic status epilepticus.

items.title: Seizure cluster on trends
items.caption: Three hours of quantitative trends: about a dozen right central seizures roughly every 11 minutes between 0:30 and 2:30, each a seizure-probability peak with a right-sided rhythmicity and spectrogram arch and a rise of the right aEEG; the left trends stay flat.

lines: FFT power: dB, using this image’s range and palette.
aEEG amplitude: µV; linear to 10 µV, logarithmic above 10 µV.
Spectrogram vertical axes: frequency in Hz.
Rhythmicity: relative score; brighter colors mean stronger rhythmicity, not dB.
Seizure probability: heuristic score from 0 to 1.
Trend time follows the labeled horizontal axis; raw EEG excerpts use seconds.

items.title: Hypsarrhythmia
items.caption: Hypsarrhythmia: very high-voltage (often >200 uV), chaotic, asynchronous delta with independent multifocal spikes and polyspikes and no organized background (20 uV/mm).

items.title: Spasm cluster on hypsarrhythmia
items.caption: Epileptic spasms in a cluster about every 10 s on a hypsarrhythmic background: each (12 s, 22 s) is a generalized high-voltage slow wave followed by a short diffuse attenuation with low-voltage fast activity and a burst of muscle artifact.

items.title: Tonic seizure
items.caption: A tonic seizure: diffuse electrodecrement at 4-5.5 s, then generalized paroxysmal fast activity building in voltage over both hemispheres, overlaid by tonic muscle artifact in the temporal chains.

items.title: 26 weeks PMA: trace discontinu
items.caption: Extreme prematurity (26 weeks PMA): high-voltage bursts of delta with superimposed fast activity separated by long, very low-voltage interburst intervals (normal discontinuity for this age).

items.title: 30 weeks PMA: discontinuous with central brushes
items.caption: 30 weeks PMA: discontinuous record, bursts of several seconds separated by low-voltage interburst intervals shorter than at 26 weeks; central delta brushes (fast activity riding a delta wave at C3/C4) sit within the bursts.

items.title: 34 weeks PMA: delta brushes on a continuous background
items.caption: 34 weeks PMA, awake/active-sleep-like continuous background: lower-voltage mixed activity with temporal delta brushes, showing a slow wave with riding 10–20 Hz fast activity and phase reversal at T3 or T4.

items.title: Term (40 weeks): continuous background
items.caption: Term neonate (40 weeks PMA): continuous mixed-frequency activity (activite moyenne) of 25-50 uV, symmetric and synchronous, without long interburst periods.

items.title: Trace alternant (term quiet sleep)
items.caption: Term quiet sleep: 3-8 s bursts of high-voltage delta alternate with 25-50 uV mixed theta-delta interburst periods of similar length; the interburst is lower but not suppressed.

items.title: Excessive discontinuity at term
items.caption: A 39-week neonate with interburst intervals longer than 6 s and interburst voltage under 25 uV: excessively discontinuous for age.

items.title: Delta brushes (32 weeks)
items.caption: Delta brushes at 32 weeks PMA: high-voltage 0.5-1.5 Hz delta waves carrying 10-20 Hz fast activity, occipito-temporal at this age, phase-reversing at T4 (Fp2-T4 against T4-O2, 5 s and 11 s) and at T3 (Fp1-T3 against T3-O1, 7 s and 9 s).

items.title: Encoches frontales (36 weeks)
items.caption: Frontal sharp transients (encoches frontales): biphasic, 50-150 uV, bilateral and roughly synchronous sharp waves at Fp1/Fp2, normal from 34-35 weeks PMA to term.

items.title: Anterior slow dysrhythmia (38 weeks)
items.caption: Runs of 1.5-2 Hz, 50-100 uV frontal delta (anterior slow dysrhythmia), a normal pattern often seen during transitional sleep near term. Behavioral state is not established by this illustrative excerpt.

items.title: Temporal theta (29 weeks)
items.caption: Temporal theta bursts at 29 weeks PMA: brief 4–6 Hz rhythmic runs with a left temporal maximum at T3, riding within bursts of a discontinuous background; typical of 26–32 weeks PMA.

items.title: Sharp theta on the occipitals (STOP), 24 weeks
items.caption: Sharp theta on the occipitals of prematurity (STOP) at 24 weeks PMA: brief 5-6 Hz sharply contoured theta runs at O1 (T3-O1, C3-O1) near 4, 7 and 16 s, within the bursts of a discontinuous record.

items.title: Neonatal focal clonic seizure
items.caption: Neonatal seizure: rhythmic 1-1.5 Hz sharp delta at C3 in the left central chain, lasting well over 10 s, with a focal clonic correlate.

items.title: Neonatal electrographic seizure (right temporal)
items.caption: Electrographic-only neonatal seizure 35 s after onset: rhythmic 2-3 Hz sharply contoured activity throughout the page in the right temporal chain (Fp2-T4, T4-O2) and C4-T4, absent on the left (the transient at 13.5 s over T3 is a delta brush).

items.title: Brief rhythmic discharge (BRD)
items.caption: A 6-s evolving rhythmic run at C3 in a term neonate: shorter than the 10-s neonatal seizure minimum, so a brief rhythmic discharge rather than a seizure.

items.title: Neonatal burst suppression
items.caption: Term neonate with burst suppression: high-voltage abnormal bursts separated by very low-voltage intervals. On this page, the central interburst intervals measure under 5 uV peak-to-peak after display filtering. Normal neonatal graphoelements are absent; this excerpt does not establish full-record invariance.

items.title: aEEG during therapeutic hypothermia
items.caption: Six hours of aEEG in an authored term-neonate HIE/cooling scenario: a discontinuous normal-voltage pattern, with an upper margin mostly 15–30 uV and intermittent higher peaks, a lower margin below 5 uV, and absent sleep-wake cycling.

lines: aEEG amplitude: µV; linear to 10 µV, logarithmic above 10 µV.
Trend time follows the labeled horizontal axis; raw EEG excerpts use seconds.

items.title: LPDs, left temporal, 1 Hz
items.caption: Lateralized periodic discharges at about 1 Hz over the left temporal chain (Fp1-F7, F7-T3, T3-T5): sharp, surface-negative discharges, each followed by a slow wave, on a low-voltage slow, unreactive background. The right hemisphere is spared.

items.title: LPDs+F, left hemisphere
items.caption: Left hemispheric LPDs at about 1 Hz with a burst of low-voltage fast activity (about 14 Hz) riding on each discharge (+F). The plus modifier makes the pattern more ictal-appearing and places it on the ictal-interictal continuum.

items.title: LPDs+R, right temporal
items.caption: Right temporal LPDs at about 0.8 Hz (F8-T4, T4-T6) with superimposed rhythmic delta near 1 Hz that is not time-locked to the discharges (+R), best seen in Fp2-F8 and T6-O2.

items.title: LPDs with a tangential dipole, referential
items.caption: Left temporal LPDs on an ipsilateral-ear referential montage: each discharge is surface-negative (upward) and maximal at T3, with an opposite, positive (downward) pole at Fp1 - a tangential dipole (ACNS polarity minor modifier).

items.title: BIPDs, independent left and right temporal
items.caption: Bilateral independent periodic discharges: left and right temporal periodic discharges, each near 1 Hz but at different rates and not time-locked to each other, so their timing drifts across the page.

items.title: GPDs, 2 Hz, frontally predominant
items.caption: Generalized periodic discharges at about 2 Hz, bisynchronous, largest in the frontal and central derivations and smallest in the occipital links, with a diffusely slow, unreactive background between them.

items.title: GPDs+F
items.caption: Generalized periodic discharges at about 1 Hz, each carrying superimposed fast activity (+F).

items.title: GPDs with triphasic morphology and A-P lag
items.caption: Blunt generalized periodic discharges at about 1.8 Hz with triphasic morphology (small negative, dominant positive, then slower negative phase) and an anterior-to-posterior lag: each complex appears in the frontal derivations before the occipital ones.

tags.acns: GPDs with triphasic morphology, A-P lag, 1.8 Hz

items.title: LPDs, spiky sharpness
items.caption: Left temporal LPDs at about 0.8 Hz whose dominant phase is spiky (under 70 ms at the baseline); the 10-second page spreads each discharge so its narrow base is easy to judge. Compare with the blunt example.

items.title: LPDs, blunt sharpness
items.caption: Left temporal LPDs at about 0.9 Hz drawn blunt: rounded discharges with a broad base, still periodic with a clear interval between them and confined to the left temporal chain. Compare with the spiky example.

items.title: LRDA, left temporal, 1.5 Hz
items.caption: Lateralized rhythmic delta activity at about 1.5 Hz over the left frontotemporal chain (Fp1-F7, F7-T3, T3-T5): a continuous train of uniform delta waves with no interval between them and no evolution in frequency or location.

items.title: LRDA+S
items.caption: Left temporal rhythmic delta at about 1.3-1.5 Hz with sharp waves embedded in the delta train (+S), seen as narrow transients on the rising phase in F7-T3 and T3-T5.

items.title: LRDA+F
items.caption: Left temporal rhythmic delta at about 1.6 Hz with superimposed fast activity near 13 Hz (+F) riding on each delta wave. Lateralized RDA above 1 Hz with a plus modifier falls on the ictal-interictal continuum.

items.title: LRDA, fluctuating
items.caption: Left temporal LRDA whose frequency changes repeatedly by at least 0.5 Hz within the page, up and down, without a sustained trend (fluctuating, not evolving). A 30-second page shows the changes.

items.title: GRDA, frontally predominant
items.caption: Generalized rhythmic delta activity at about 2 Hz, bisynchronous, largest in the frontal and frontocentral derivations and smallest in the occipital links, filling the page without evolution.

items.title: GRDA, occipitally predominant (OIRDA-like)
items.caption: Generalized rhythmic delta at about 3 Hz with an occipital predominance: largest in P3-O1, P4-O2, T5-O1 and T6-O2 on the longitudinal bipolar montage.

items.title: Extreme delta brush
items.caption: Continuous, frontally predominant rhythmic delta at about 1.5 Hz with 20-30 Hz fast activity riding on each delta wave (extreme delta brush, a form of RDA+F).

items.title: BIRDs, right temporal
items.caption: A sharply contoured 6-second run of rhythmic activity above 4 Hz over the right temporal chain (F8-T4, T4-T6), starting and stopping abruptly. In the stated setting without a clinical correlate or a known benign rhythm, this illustrates possible BIRDs; brief duration alone does not define BIRDs.

items.title: SIRPIDs after sternal rub
items.caption: Generalized periodic discharges at about 1.3 Hz that begin about 3 s after a sternal rub (marked) and are absent before it: stimulus-induced (SI-) GPDs, SIRPIDs.

items.title: LPDs evolving into an electrographic seizure
items.caption: Left temporal LPDs beginning at about 1 Hz speed up in steps to about 2 Hz and then 3 Hz while growing in voltage, and stop after about 23 s. Definite evolution lasting 10 s or more meets ACNS criterion B for an electrographic seizure.

items.title: GPDs at 3 Hz (criterion A seizure)
items.caption: Generalized sharp periodic discharges at about 3 Hz, frontocentrally maximal and sustained across the page: epileptiform discharges averaging more than 2.5 Hz for 10 s or more meet ACNS criterion A for an electrographic seizure, even without evolution.

items.title: Normal term aEEG with sleep-wake cycling
items.caption: Term neonatal aEEG (day 3), predominantly continuous normal voltage: the lower margin is generally around or above 5 uV and the upper margin well above 10 uV, with brief lower-margin dips. Sleep-wake cycling appears as recurring 15-30-minute stretches of band widening and lower-margin dips toward 5 uV (quiet sleep, trace alternant), alternating with narrower continuous stretches.

items.title: Discontinuous normal voltage aEEG
items.caption: Discontinuous normal voltage aEEG: the lower margin is predominantly below 5 uV while the upper margin stays above 10 uV, with a broad band and no clear mature sleep-wake cycling. The raw strip shows a burst followed by a lower-voltage interval.

items.title: Burst-suppression aEEG
items.caption: Burst-suppression aEEG: the lower margin sits at 1-2 uV and the upper margin near 25-30 uV, a band with no sleep-wake cycling. The raw strip shows brief bursts separated by suppressed intervals of several seconds.

items.title: Recurrent neonatal seizures on aEEG
items.caption: Continuous normal voltage aEEG with five abrupt rises of the lower and upper margins on the left channel (C3-P3), each lasting a few minutes: recurrent electrographic seizures. The right channel (C4-P4) does not change. The raw strip is taken during the fourth seizure and shows rhythmic delta.

items.title: Left hemispheric seizures on CSA, aEEG and envelope
items.caption: Four hours of trends with three left hemispheric seizures: each shows on the left FFT spectrogram as a bright streak sweeping down from about 4 Hz to 1.5 Hz, with a matching rise of the left aEEG band and envelope and a brief postictal dip. The right-sided trends change far less.

items.title: Rhythmicity and seizure probability with focal seizures
items.caption: Four right temporal seizures appear as seizure-probability peaks aligned with brief streaks on the right rhythmicity and right FFT spectrograms; the asymmetry index swings toward the right (+) with each one while the left trends stay unchanged.

items.caption: Continuous left temporal LPDs at 1 Hz leave the seizure-probability trace flat and add only a faint harmonic comb on the spectrogram; the real seizure at 150 min stands out as a probability peak, a rhythmicity band and an evolving CSA arc.

items.caption: Electrographic status epilepticus for 90 minutes: sustained rhythmicity and a spectrogram band that wanders in frequency and waxes and wanes in power, then slows, fragments and fades out over the last minutes rather than stopping abruptly.

items.caption: A persistent right hemispheric attenuation holds the asymmetry index near -40 to -50% (left greater than right) for the whole record, and the relative asymmetry spectrogram is blue (left-greater), most intensely in the delta-theta band. items.caption: Burst suppression deepens in two steps after pentobarbital increases at 40 and 95 min: the bilateral suppression ratio climbs from about 25% to 55% and then to about 80%, the top of the shaded 60-80% target band. items.caption: After a dexmedetomidine increase at 90 min, the alpha/delta ratio falls on both sides together and a 12-16 Hz spindle-like band appears on both FFT spectrograms, a symmetric, sleep-like drug effect rather than a focal change. Total power changes little.

items.title: Typical absence
items.caption: Generalized 3-Hz spike-and-wave, faster at onset and slowing toward 2.5 Hz, frontal maximum, abrupt onset and offset; the background returns at once.

items.title: Atypical absence
items.caption: Slow (<2.5 Hz), irregular sharp-and-slow-wave complexes with gradual onset and offset on a slow background; the sharp component precedes each slow wave. Average reference exposes the preceding sharp component in the frontocentral channels and the subsequent slower wave; the background is diffusely slow.

items.title: Myoclonic seizure
items.caption: Brief generalized polyspike-and-wave, frontocentral maximum, each with a short burst of scalp muscle (the jerk).

items.title: Myoclonic-atonic seizure
items.caption: Polyspike-and-wave followed by a larger slow wave while the EMG row falls silent (loss of tone).

items.title: Myoclonic-tonic seizure
items.caption: A myoclonic polyspike-and-wave that runs into low-voltage fast activity with tonic EMG.

items.title: Tonic seizure
items.caption: A diffuse high-voltage sharp-and-slow wave, then electrodecrement and bisynchronous 15-25 Hz paroxysmal fast activity building in voltage, frontally predominant, with tonic EMG.

items.title: Atonic seizure
items.caption: A single vertex-maximal sharp-and-slow wave with an abrupt silent period on the EMG row.

items.title: GTC - onset and tonic phase
items.caption: Low-voltage fast activity recruiting into a high-voltage ~10-Hz rhythm under muscle that soon obscures every derivation except the vertex.

items.title: GTC - clonic phase
items.caption: Polyspike bursts locked to muscle bursts, separated by near-flat intervals that lengthen as the bursts slow; electrode movement with each jerk.

items.title: GTC - end and postictal suppression
items.caption: The last discharges come further apart (here they fade), then generalized postictal suppression below 10 uV.

items.title: Eyelid myoclonia (Jeavons)
items.caption: Eye closure (Fp blink deflection), then 3-6 Hz generalized polyspike-and-wave within about a second, with repetitive eyelid-jerk artifact on the frontal poles.

items.title: Photoparoxysmal response
items.caption: Generalized 3-4 Hz spike-and-wave during an 18-Hz flash train (photic row), not locked to the flashes, stopping with the train (Waltz type 4).

items.title: Photoparoxysmal response, self-sustained
items.caption: As above, but the generalized discharge outlasts the flash train by 1-3 s.

items.title: Interictal generalized spike-wave
items.caption: Brief bursts of generalized 3-4 Hz spike-and-wave between normal background.

items.title: Interictal polyspike-wave (JME)
items.caption: 4-6 Hz generalized polyspike-and-wave bursts in every chain, as in juvenile myoclonic epilepsy.

items.title: Sporadic generalized polyspikes
items.caption: Isolated frontocentral polyspikes with a slow wave; each electrode has its own lag and spike heights.

items.title: Slow spike-and-wave (Lennox-Gastaut)
items.caption: Irregular 1.5-2.5 Hz sharp-and-slow-wave complexes, frontal maximum, on a slow background. Average reference exposes the preceding sharp component in the frontocentral channels and the subsequent slower wave; the background is diffusely slow.

items.title: Generalized paroxysmal fast activity (N2)
items.caption: Abrupt bisynchronous ~20 Hz bursts, frontally predominant, with the background attenuated beneath them; irregular in height and frequency, not spindle-like.

items.title: Generalized paroxysmal fast activity (N3)
items.caption: Abrupt bisynchronous ~20 Hz bursts, frontally predominant, with the background attenuated beneath them; irregular in height and frequency, not spindle-like.

items.title: ESES / CSWS in N2
items.caption: Near-continuous 1.5-2 Hz spike-and-wave in NREM sleep, centro-parietal and left-predominant.

items.title: SeLECTS / BECTS: bilateral independent centrotemporal spikes (bipolar)
items.caption: Independent left and right centrotemporal discharges on the same normal drowsy background. Negative peaks reverse at C3/T3 or C4/T4, with the frontal positive pole of a transverse dipole and an after-going slow wave. Paired with the referential view of this same recording and time window.

items.title: SeLECTS / BECTS: bilateral independent centrotemporal spikes (referential)
items.caption: The same recording and time window as the paired bipolar view, using average reference as in the ILAE example. Centrotemporal negativity at C3/T3 or C4/T4 points upward; the simultaneous frontal positive pole points downward. The left and right discharges occur independently on a normal drowsy background.

items.title: Midline theta rhythm (Ciganek)
items.caption: A waxing and waning 6 Hz midline theta train, maximal at Cz with Fz greater than Pz and only a small parasagittal field. Smooth rhythmic activity in an awake adult; a normal variant without ictal evolution.
